brief: UBS's Nov 5 cash-trading note reads the US midterms as a de-escalation signal on the Iran conflict: Polymarket's longer-dated (end-March 2027) odds on lifting the US Naval blockade are the most visible mover, up to 71% from 64%, while near-term odds barely moved. The note frames the election as a clearing event (VIX -4.5 vol) that released a technical-selling overhang, lifting risk assets (oil down, Consumer Discretionary beating Energy by 11.2%) while the 10-year yield fell to 4.85%, the dollar weakened against G10 and gold rose near $4,110, which the note reads as cross-asset confirmation of the de-escalation view; China equities (HSTECH, H shares, KWEB) rallied as a rotation beneficiary. UBS adds a conditional house view that US markets keep underperforming relatively if this reading holds. Separately, AI-linked names sold off (Neoclouds -8.4%, Asian AI-chain semis down) on rising AI-regulation risk, and Qualcomm guided below consensus and fell 7.2% after hours. UBS expects the BoE to hike 25bp to 4.0% today, with the MPC vote flipping to 7-2 for a hike and some risk of an 8-1 hawkish split. Wednesday's European cash desk flows were balanced (52/48) at roughly 2x average volume, with Banks and Tech better bought and Industrials and Energy better sold.
